# Goal entry

What a goal needs, what can’t be saved and who may save it: one rule for New goal, the edit page, set-up’s cards, a spreadsheet’s Goals rows and the AI tools, in the same words.

## The rule

Every way a goal comes in asks the same rule, in the same words: New goal, the edit page, set-up's goal cards, a Goals row of a spreadsheet, Data or a bulk edit (the change engine, `planChanges`), and the AI tools (which use the change engine). The form saves through `planGoal`, run by the `saveGoal` action, so it can't save what the engine would refuse.

**Who may (rule 7).** Anyone may add a goal for anyone, at any level, at every door (Lane, 11 Nov: `mayAddGoal` is always yes, and is the one place that is said). Changing a goal stays with its owner and admins (`mayChangeGoal`), whoever made it; New goal says so as soon as someone else is chosen as owner: “Amara will own it. After it is published, only Amara or an admin can change it.”

**What a field needs (rule 1).** Read from the spreadsheet's field table (`fieldNeed`): required, optional, worked out, or not asked for this type. In the form, a field that always shows a value (the type, the team, the level, which side a range keeps to) is required. Optional fields say “· optional” after their label; a step with two or more required fields and at least one optional says “Everything here is needed unless it says optional.” under its heading. The unit is optional and starts empty: a number has no unit by default, never “%”.

**What can't be saved (rule 2, `goalMustFix`).** Each problem is under its own field, in the form's order. The name (at least three characters), an owner, a team (“{Owner} isn’t in a team. Choose the team this goal is for.” when the owner has none), a level, a link that would make a loop; for a number to move, where it starts (“Enter where it starts today.”; on the edit page “Enter where it starts.”) and a target that differs from it (“The target is the same as today (40%). To hold a number where it is, make this a number to keep in range.”, offering to); for a range, the limit, and a warning margin of zero or more (empty is none); for a number to move, a To after its From and neither beyond the weeks offered (“To (week 40, 28 Sep–4 Oct 2026) isn’t after From (week 46, 9–15 Nov 2026). The plan has to run forwards.”); for stages, at least one, each with a name, a name no other stage has (compared without case or accents), and a due week in the year. A stage done in a check-in can't be removed, and fewer decimal places than check-ins already have is refused.

**A number as typed (rule 12, `numberAsTyped`).** Digits as people type them (a decimal comma, thousands, a sign); words after it only when they are the goal's unit (“12 days” in a days goal, with min and mins, day and days, hr and hours the same; “12%” in a % goal). Anything else after the digits is “has words”: “12 days” has words in it. Type the number only, like 12; this goal counts %. Letters in place of digits are “not a number”, with an example at the goal's decimal places.

**Decimals, worked out (`decimalsFor`).** The places chosen; or, when none were, the most typed in Today, Target or Limit, at most 3, said in one line (“Kept to 1 decimal place, as you typed them.”) with Change. A number with more places than chosen is refused, offering to keep them.

**What is asked (rule 3, `goalChecks`).** What is possible but unlikely is a question, never a refusal: a Check, in the same block as the check-in's, under the field it is about, with two answers, the first keeping what was typed. In this order, each that applies, and only once the fields it is about have no Must fix: a stage already past (“Week 43 was 2 weeks ago. Is this stage already done?”, either answer an answer); no unit (“This number has no unit. Is it a plain count?”, asked once); a number below zero for a percentage, time or money; over 100% (“The target is over 100%. That’s fine for growth, but a share of something (coverage, adoption) can’t pass 100%. Is 150% right?”); a target 100 times its start or more, or a 100th; a billion or more; a target on the worse side of the start for the metric chosen to measure it (““Pipeline queue wait” is better lower, but the target (9 min) is above today (7 min). Is that the plan?”: the metric the form chose, from the goal.measure place, else the one that measures the goal now, which a module says through its records' `measures` (`goalMeasureOf`), so the saving rule, a spreadsheet's rows and the AI tools ask it of a goal already measured); the same name in the same team; an owner in another team (“Amara is in Office of the VP, not Build & Release. Which team is this goal for?”, whose second answer moves it); a link to a goal at a lower level (whose second answer removes the link); a warning margin as wide as the limit; weeks set by hand that leave more than 60% of the change to the last quarter of the plan's weeks (`lateShare`); and, for a goal being changed, a target that flips which way is better or a number far outside the old plan (`planQuestion`). An answer is kept in the draft as the values it was about (`answers[slot] = key`), so changing them asks again (`unanswered`, shared with the check-in); answered, the block collapses to “You said 150% is right.” with Change. A goal already saved isn't asked again about what it already says. The import asks the same questions in the same words (an unlikely number, a link to a lower level), keeping its own forms of no unit, the same name and stages already past; a file's Team column says the team in so many words, so an owner in another team is asked only in the form. The AI tools list every question goal by goal (“Not saved. Check with the person first: …”) and take `confirm: true` as yes to each. About a number goal's weeks (the [years and weeks](years-and-weeks.md) rules): a From before this week (“Week 40 was 6 weeks ago. Has this been running since then? The plan would expect 39 min by this week.”, whose second answer starts it this week), a To already past, and a plan longer than 53 weeks; a file is asked only the last. The question about a metric's latest number (`far-from-metric`) waits for the metrics module to keep one for a slice; a file is asked `wrong-side` once the import reads Measured by.

**Whether a step goes on (rule 4, `stepState`).** The button is never disabled. Pressed with a Must fix on its step, every field of the step shows its own, focus goes to the first, and one line above the button counts them: “2 things to fix above: Unit and Target.” (more than three: the first two “and {k} more”), the same line the check-in uses. A Must fix shows under a field once it has been changed and left, never while typing. With none, an unanswered question holds the step: focus goes to it and the line reads “Answer the question above, under Target.” (several: “Answer the 2 questions above.”; `openLine`). The edit page's Save changes does the same.

**Saving (rule 7, `planGoal`).** Refused, in these words, unless the actor may, nothing must be fixed, every question is answered (“Not saved. Check with the person first: …”, with the questions' words), and a plan change after check-ins have started has a reason (“Say why, in a sentence. It goes in the goal’s History, and anyone watching it sees the change flagged.”). Then one commit: the goal (a new one with the workspace's next key), its History entry with Why and each answer as *Checked* (the question, then the answer given), and a new goal's stages already done (only those due before this week, whatever the draft says).

## Limits the records hold

Faro’s database holds these as well as the rule; a rebuild holds them wherever it stores the records. The constraint names are in `spec/core/schema.sql`, which is for reading, not copying.

- A goal’s title has at least 3 characters (spaces at either end not counted). (`okr_goals_title_check`; the code holds it too, in `src/domain/thresholds.ts`)
- A goal keeps 0 to 3 decimal places. (A metric may keep 4: a goal measured by it keeps fewer, and is warned.) (`okr_goals_decimals_check`)
- A number goal has a start, a target and a plan shape, and its start and target differ. (`okr_goals_check`)
- A range goal has a bound (at most or at least), a limit and a warning margin. (`okr_goals_check1`)
- A range goal kept between two numbers has a lower number below its limit; any other range goal has no lower number. (`okr_goals_range_lower_ok`)
- A range goal’s warning margin is 0 or more. (`okr_goals_range_margin_check`)
- A headline goal feeds nothing. (`okr_goals_check2`)

## Requirements

- `GOAL-ENTRY-REQUIRED`: Every way of adding a goal says what it needs before it is refused, checks it with one rule, and asks rather than assumes where a value is possible but unlikely; nothing is saved before it has been read back.
